skill.description: Run structured quality verification across static analysis, dynamic testing, integration checks, and release certification gates.

skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline backticks, local report reads, and sample report text. Real risks remain around private-key signing, unpinned alpha package execution, and pre-filled approval language that could be used without evidence.

remediation.issue: Private-key signing command in certification workflow
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before signing, keep private keys outside the repository, and prefer a managed CI signing service or documented secure key path.
Pin the package to a reviewed version, document the source, and require confirmation before downloading or running third-party packages.
Convert approval statements into placeholders and require evidence links, reviewer names, timestamps, and real gate results before release certification.

remediation.issue: Operational command examples in marketplace skill documentation
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as examples, list prerequisites, and instruct agents to ask before running project scripts, scanners, local service checks, or report generation.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Alpha Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly instructs users to run npx claude-flow@alpha. That can download and execute a moving third-party package version during quality verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is explicit in both primary workflow documentation files and uses the alpha tag instead of a pinned version. The risk is supply-chain exposure, not evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Pre-Filled Release Approval Claims
semantic_findings.description: The templates include approval language such as Security Team approved and approved for production release. If copied without evidence, this can misrepresent release governance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files show explicit approval and compliance text inside report templates. The context is documentation, so the finding is governance risk rather than direct malware behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent release checks before code reaches production. This skill organizes static analysis, tests, integration validation, certification, and reports into one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines a five-phase workflow for static analysis, dynamic testing, integration validation, certification, and reporting.
Provides example commands for SonarQube, ESLint, TypeScript, Jest, Cypress, Playwright, Pact, and Newman.
Specifies measurable thresholds for maintainability, complexity, coverage, pass rates, and integration health.
Lists expected report artifacts, audit trails, certification files, and stakeholder outputs.
Coordinates the code-analyzer, tester, and production-validator roles through claude-flow hook examples.
limitations: It does not include runnable implementation scripts; the target project must provide matching commands and configuration.
Example metrics and approval text must be replaced with real evidence from the current build.
Some checks require local services, third-party tools, or CI permissions that may not exist in every project.
External commands and signing steps require user review before execution in sensitive repositories.

use_cases.title: Audit a Release Candidate
use_cases.description: Run static checks, tests, integration validation, and certification before a release branch is approved.

use_cases.title: Build CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Convert the workflow into CI stages that fail builds when quality scores or coverage targets are missed.

use_cases.title: Prepare Stakeholder Reports
use_cases.description: Generate evidence-based summaries for quality, security, performance, and compliance review meetings.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Quality Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my project quality. Start with static analysis and tell me which commands you need before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Review Test Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate unit, integration, and end-to-end test results. Summarize failures, flaky tests, coverage gaps, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Release Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to check release gates for this branch. Compare the evidence against thresholds and identify blockers before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a CI quality verification workflow for my repository. Include phases, required tools, artifacts, thresholds, and manual approval points.

output_examples.input: Review this release candidate for quality readiness.
output_examples.output: The release is not ready. Static analysis passed, but integration validation found three failed checks. Fix the webhook race condition before approval.

output_examples.input: Summarize the quality gate results for stakeholders.
output_examples.output: The report lists gate status, coverage results, failed tests, service health, known risks, and the evidence needed for sign-off.

output_examples.input: Help me convert this process into CI steps.
output_examples.output: Recommended stages are install, static analysis, dynamic tests, integration validation, certification scoring, artifact upload, and manual approval.

best_practices: Run the workflow in a clean branch with project-specific tool configuration already committed.
Replace every sample approval, score, and compliance claim with evidence from the current build.
Review all external commands, package downloads, and signing operations before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample certification text as real stakeholder approval.
Do not run unreviewed project scripts or package downloads in a sensitive environment.
Do not publish quality reports that omit failed tests, flaky tests, or known issues.

faq.question: Does this skill run the quality tools by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and command examples. The project must include the tools, scripts, services, and configuration.

faq.question: Which tools does the workflow mention?
faq.answer: It references SonarQube, ESLint, TypeScript, Jest, Cypress, Playwright, Pact, Newman, and claude-flow hooks.

faq.question: Can it certify a production release?
faq.answer: It can structure certification evidence. Real release approval must come from verified test results and authorized stakeholders.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes, if the repository provides matching scripts and the team reviews command execution, artifacts, and failure thresholds.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm package sources, local service requirements, signing key handling, and whether the sample thresholds match your risk policy.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It includes security compliance checks, but teams still need evidence-based security review and approval.
